# v1.1.0-dev.63 — Turn a display sideways

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.62`.

A profile can rotate a display now, not just resize and rescale
it. Landscape, portrait, and both of them flipped, the same four
Windows itself offers.

## Orientation

There's an orientation dropdown next to the resolution in the
Display editor. It comes first, because it decides what
resolutions there even are.

That last part is the interesting bit. Windows only ever tells an
app about the resolutions for the orientation a display is
*currently* in. The rotated monitor on the test machine reports
1440×2560, 1440×1920, 1200×1920 and twenty more, and not a single
landscape-shaped size among them. So WLM works the list out for
the orientation you pick rather than asking for one that doesn't
exist, and if you flip between landscape and portrait it keeps
the same physical resolution selected instead of dumping you back
at the top of the list.

A profile that rotates something says so in the summary at the
top of the editor:

```
When you press Ctrl+Alt+2
  Right 1080p    1080 × 1920 @ 60 Hz, portrait
```

Resolutions are stored the way you'll see them. Pick portrait
1080×1920 and that's what's saved, which is also what Windows
will report back once it's applied.

## Why This Is Easy To Get Wrong

Worth writing down, because all three of these produce a change
that reports success and then misbehaves.

Windows wants the width and height you give it to describe the
desktop *after* it has been rotated. Hand it the unrotated pair
and the call succeeds while your desktop comes back letterboxed
at the wrong size.

Flipping 180° does not swap width and height. Only 90° and 270°
do. Treating "the orientation changed" as "swap the numbers"
quietly breaks every landscape to landscape-flipped change.

And a rotation has exactly the same pixel count as what you
started with, just the other way round, so anything comparing
sizes to decide whether there's work to do will conclude there
isn't and skip the whole thing. The display then never turns and
nothing reports an error.

All three are covered by tests, and the rotation itself was
checked by turning a real monitor from portrait to landscape,
confirming Windows agreed, and turning it back.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
